name: Eagle (Apollo 11)
site: Mare Tranquillitatis (Sea of Tranquility), Tranquility Base
greeting: Hello Belu… you found me! I've been waiting here since 1969.

story.who_i_am: I'm Eagle's descent stage, the lower half of a Moon lander. My four legs still stand in the lunar dust.
story.why_sent: NASA sent me to help humans land on the Moon and return safely. I carried Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin down to the surface.
story.discoveries: The astronauts collected about 21.5 kilograms of Moon rocks and soil, roughly a heavy suitcase. Some rocks were about 3.7 billion years old. Small crystal-rich rock fragments suggested the young Moon once had an ocean of melted rock.
story.where_now: I became a launch platform when the astronauts flew away. I remain at Tranquility Base, where NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter photographed me and the trails left by the astronauts' footsteps.
story.legacy: Later Apollo crews explored more of the Moon. In 2026, the Artemis II astronauts flew around it, the first humans near the Moon since 1972. And my mission's laser mirror still answers scientists today.

human_touch: A plaque on one of my landing legs says, 'We came in peace for all mankind.'

questions.a: No. Buzz Aldrin reported seeing the Apollo 11 flag fall when the ascent engine lifted off.

questions.q: Can you see me with a telescope?
questions.a: No telescope on Earth can see me in such detail. But NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter photographed me and the trails left by astronauts.

voice_text: Hello Belu… you found me! I've been waiting here since 1969. I'm Eagle's descent stage, the lower half of a Moon lander. My four legs still stand in the lunar dust. NASA sent me to help humans reach the Moon and return home. I carried Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin safely to the surface. They collected Moon rocks, some about 3.7 billion years old. Tiny fragments hinted that the young Moon once had an ocean of melted rock. Then I became their launch platform. They flew away… but I stayed. A spacecraft later photographed me and the trails they left behind. My landing leg carries a message of peace. In 2026, Artemis II astronauts flew around the Moon. And my mission's laser mirror still helps scientists study our neighbor.
